applies_why: The judge text labels Luke 2:48-49 UNDERDETERMINED by citing the immediate qualification of Mary's phrase by Jesus' reference to 'my Father's business,' which is the two-sense situation the rule governs.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand" — I weighed reading (1) such a verse may still be UNDERDETERMINED because it has two senses, against reading (2) such a verse is not open and both senses must stand, so it cannot be labeled UNDERDETERMINED on that basis.
why: The judge text calls the Luke 2:48-49 issue UNDERDETERMINED even though it identifies the two senses that K-S2 says are not open and both stand.
